name: Structure of Partial Cubes with At Most Two Excess Vertices
statement: A connected partial cube of isometric dimension $d$ has at least $d+1$ vertices. Equality holds exactly in the tree case. If it has $d+2$ vertices, it is unicyclic and its unique cycle is a square. Consequently every nontrivial partial cube with at most $d+2$ vertices has a peripheral coordinate.
proof: Reverse a complete sequence of $d$ coordinate contractions and let $s_i$ be the order of the site duplicated by expansion $i$. Then $|V|=1+\sum_i s_i$ and the excess over $d+1$ is $\sum_i(s_i-1)$. Zero excess makes every new coordinate a bridge and yields a tree. Excess one permits exactly one two-vertex site; it is an edge in the preceding tree, its duplication creates one square, and all later singleton-site expansions attach bridges. A leaf edge is peripheral, while every coordinate of a bare square is peripheral.
